tool.name: method_tamper_check
tool.description:
Probe a URL for HTTP verb / method tampering vulnerabilities. Bundles 4 deterministic checks plus an opt-in destructive cohort:
**Default (read-only) cohort** — always runs: - `OPTIONS` — discovers Allow-header advertisement; flags WebDAV verbs (PROPFIND/MOVE/COPY/MKCOL/LOCK/UNLOCK) → medium CWE-200 webdav_exposure; flags advertised modifying methods (PUT/PATCH/DELETE) → low CWE-200 method_disclosure. - `TRACE` with custom request header → if response is 2xx and body reflects the custom header, XST primitive confirmed → medium CWE-200 xst. - `HEAD` — compared to GET. If GET returns 2xx but HEAD returns 405/501 → low CWE-200 method_disclosure (cache asymmetry). - `PROPFIND` — if response is 207 Multi-Status (or 200 with XML Content-Type), WebDAV is wired up to this URL → medium CWE-200 webdav_exposure (deduped against the OPTIONS-advertised case).
**Destructive cohort** — only runs when `include_destructive=True`: - `X-HTTP-Method-Override: PUT/PATCH/DELETE` (POST with the override header) — if 2xx/3xx, framework respects override → high CWE-285 improper_authorization. - `_method=PUT/DELETE` form parameter (POST with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) — if 2xx/3xx, framework respects form-based override → high. - Direct `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` to the URL — if 2xx/3xx, route handler accepts state-changing methods → high.
Per-class dedup on destructive findings: 3 override variants → ONE finding; 3 direct-verb variants → ONE finding; 2 form-method variants → ONE finding.
Severity tuning: - **High** (CWE-285, improper_authorization) — destructive verb (direct or via override) returns 2xx/3xx on documented-GET endpoint. - **Medium** (CWE-200) — TRACE-with-reflection (XST), WebDAV-advertised, PROPFIND-succeeds. - **Low** (CWE-200) — OPTIONS reveals modifying methods; HEAD returns 405/501 vs GET 200.
Skip cases: - Baseline GET non-2xx/3xx → endpoint can't be measured → graceful inconclusive. - Cluster-A `--exclude-path` blocks the URL → graceful no-op.
**Safety**: - Read-only by default. `include_destructive=True` requires explicit operator consent — direct PUT/PATCH/DELETE and method-override probes can mutate state on a vulnerable target. - Cluster-A `--exclude-path` is the primary safety lever for blocking probes against specific endpoints. - All probes carry `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (implement explicit method allow-list at the route handler; strip `X-HTTP-Method-Override` and similar headers at the edge; disable TRACE; deploy WebDAV on a separate origin if needed) and `verification_status=needs_review` since 2xx-on-DELETE doesn't necessarily mean the resource was actually deleted (the framework may return 200 for an unhandled method).
Composes with cluster-A safety: `--exclude-path` / `--rate-limit` / `--auth-*` apply to every probe.

parameter.name: target_url
parameter.description: URL to probe. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Examples: `https://app.example.com/api/users/123`, `https://api.example.com/v1/profile`, `https://app.example.com/admin/`.

parameter.name: include_destructive
parameter.description: Whether to run the destructive cohort (X-HTTP-Method-Override / _method form / direct PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Default `False` (read-only cohort only). Set `True` only on staging targets where the operator has explicitly consented to state-changing probes.

returns.description:
{success, target_url, target_host, include_destructive, baseline: {status, status_class, body_length, error?, skipped?}, options_advertised: [method, ...], probes: [{label, method, class_, status, body_length, headers_subset, evidence, finding_severity}, ...], findings_emitted}.
The agent should follow up high-severity destructive-verb findings by checking whether the request actually mutated state (was the resource really deleted? did the new value persist?) before treating the finding as a confirmed exploit.
